correctness.rationale: For A invertible, nonzero squares are nonzero and one-dimensional subalgebras are precisely Frobenius-semilinear projective fixed lines. Two fixed lines give exactly one more by the equation s lambda1=t lambda2, including q=2. The single-line incidence count totals N and the pair count totals N/2; because r is 0,1,3 the fibers must have sizes N/3,N/2,N/6. Explicit field arithmetic enumerates all GL2(q) for q=2,4,8,16 and confirms the formula. No finite enumeration is used as a general proof.

value.rationale: The number of nonzero subalgebra lines is a basic intrinsic algebra invariant, equivalently the number of nonzero idempotents for a perfect algebra. The theorem gives its entire fiber distribution across every labeled binary perfect evolution algebra over any even finite field; a sharp one-third zero-subalgebra stratum is a structural finite-field contrast with complex-field existence, and the exact invariant is not an arbitrary parameter slice. It is not claimed as a class-count theorem or a paper-sized contribution.
